annual.comparability_note: 2021 IPO/share class conversions make weighted-average share counts incomparable with end-of-period shares. Loss includes 2,045 change in fair value of convertible notes/warrant liability; 2021 IPO recognition included approximately 1,010 SBC.
SBC includes 485 charge related to cancellation of 2021 founders market-based RSUs. FY2025 presentation separates credit loss provision from operations; total opex unchanged.
2024 GAAP net income includes a 347 tax benefit; deferred-tax valuation allowance release makes headline net margin non-recurring.
2025 effective tax rate 10.7%; tax-rate reconciliation includes 184 SBC tax benefit and 66 research/development tax credits.

balance_sheet.parent_cash_limitation: Only consolidated cash is disclosed in selected latest materials; do not relabel 5829 as parent-company freely distributable or excess cash.
balance_sheet.customer_platform_assets_treatment: Customer metric, not an enterprise asset or additive equity value; users own securities. Off-balance sheet customer crypto custody 37900.

regulatory_capital.status: Disclosed entities compliant at period end; net capital and requirements fluctuate daily.
regulatory_capital.interpretation: Regulatory excess capital is not synonymous with freely withdrawable cash. Clearing collateral, operating liquidity, loan growth, covenant thresholds, other jurisdictions and stress buffers must be provided before any extraction. Do not add this table to B0 or cash.

convertible.conversion_principal_settlement: cash required up to principal; excess may be cash/shares/combination

debt.warehouse_classification: Other current liabilities; separate from 2660 long-term borrowings and separate from ABS.
debt.credit_card_trust_creditors_recourse: No recourse to general credit; trust assets settle trust obligations. Exposure includes trust net assets and expected credit losses.

postperiod_event_2026_10_15.note: Subsequent event, not included in September 30 balance. Do not add entire amount as net incremental debt without knowing warehouse repayments.

debt.valuation_treatment: RIM starts with parent book equity already net of all reported liabilities. Do not again subtract convertible/ABS debt or add consolidated cash. For EV-style analysis, separate financing of earning assets from general corporate debt and exclude customer payables/collateral from ordinary industrial debt. For converts, do not both deduct full debt and add all as-converted shares; model mandatory cash principal and share/capped-call excess consistently.

shares_and_compensation.TradePMR_shares_note: Already issued/outstanding; do not add again to current issued shares.
shares_and_compensation.interpretation: Recurring SBC is an economic labor expense. Adding it back while ignoring dilution or offsetting repurchase cost overstates per-share value. Current diluted EPS denominator is period-weighted and does not contain antidilutive convert shares; future authorized shares are not all presently issued dilution.

clean_surplus_bridge.note: Capped-call cash payment 123.2 differs from net equity-statement reduction 93; use reported equity bridge, not cash outflow, when reconciling B0. A net-income-only retained-earnings book roll-forward is not actual clean surplus when these direct equity/owner transactions continue. OCI should be zero only as an explicit forecast assumption.

cashflow_quality.warning: These are consolidated cash-accounting flows, not owner earnings. Net customer funding changes and restricted/segregated movements dominate CFO; loan origination purchases are in investing CF, and financing proceeds are not distributable earnings.

credit_and_capital_needs.coastal_bank_off_balance_risk: Receivables and bank funding are not on the balance sheet; Robinhood bears losses under program terms. Bank legal ownership does not remove Robinhood economic credit risk.
credit_and_capital_needs.interpretation: 9M card provisions 143 exceed card net interest 122; Q3 provisions 61 exceed card net interest 50. This comparison excludes card noninterest revenue and operating/rewards/network expenses, so it is a warning about immature earnings and credit cost, not a full segment-profit calculation. Margin lending and customer collateral require liquidity and risk capital; customer collateral itself is not enterprise wealth.

nonoperating_tax_and_amendment.RVII_management_fee: 2% NAV plus 20% incentive fee on realized capital gains
nonoperating_tax_and_amendment.amended_adjusted_earnings_bridge_Q3: 468 + 2 CFO/restructuring SBC + 67 investment losses + 9 acquired-intangible amortization - 4 tax impact = 542
nonoperating_tax_and_amendment.amendment_reason: 8-K/A solely revises tax effect presentation of non-GAAP adjustments; GAAP unchanged. 550 to 542 is not a new 8 NCI adjustment.
nonoperating_tax_and_amendment.valuation_interpretation: Strip nonrecurring investment/deconsolidation effects for normal operating earnings and set a defensible through-cycle tax rate. Retained fund fair values are already in B0; do not add them again in RIM. In sum-of-parts, remove related earnings and capital before adding investment value separately.

acquisitions.note: TradePMR 169 cash plus 100 postclose employment compensation must not be mislabeled 269 acquisition consideration; employee service cost is SBC. Business combinations bring customer cash AND offsetting customer obligations. Acquired segregated customer funds are not cash windfalls.

limitations: No independently disclosed current parent-only freely distributable cash figure found in selected latest filings; consolidated cash is not sufficient to infer excess cash.

Regulatory capital table covers named US entities; other jurisdictions/crypto licenses and business stress buffers may require more capital. Minimum regulatory capital is not a sufficient estimate of optimal operating capital.
Cash capex does not distinguish maintenance versus growth. Internally developed software capitalization and capitalized SBC should remain explicit.
TTM and annual values use reported rounded millions. TTM is a derived period, not a management forecast. No share price or investment recommendation is supplied by this evidence file.

2025 annual cash-flow reconciliation comparative cash balances as rendered via text preprocessing show historical-period values that do not readily reconcile with the 2023 original report. Historical cash-balance series has deliberately not been constructed from that table. Core income/CFO/capex and latest Q3 balance sheet are separately identified; this is not evidence of financial misstatement.

Latest segregated aggregate includes cash and securities, whereas the CFS reconciliation is cash/equivalents only. Do not treat their difference, or the full segregated aggregate, as excess corporate cash. Selected fair-value tables should not be used as a complete allocation of that aggregate without full ledger detail.

NOTE 11: FINANCING ACTIVITIES AND OFF-BALANCE SHEET RISK
Convertible Notes
On June 25, 2026, we issued $2.2 billion aggregate principal amount of 0.00% convertible senior notes due 2029 pursuant to an indenture between RHM and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, as trustee, in a private offering pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act. The Convertible Notes are senior unsecured obligations of RHM. The $2.2 billion aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes included $200 million in aggregate principal amount of Notes issued pursuant to the initial purchasers’ option to purchase additional Convertible Notes on the same terms and conditions, which the initial purchasers exercised in full on June 23, 2026. The Convertible Notes do not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the Notes will not accrete. The Convertible Notes will mature on October 1, 2029, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed, or converted. We may pay special interest on the Notes under certain circumstances in accordance with the terms of the Indenture.
In connection with the offering of the Convertible Notes, we used approximately $290 million of the net proceeds from the offering of the Convertible Notes to repurchase approximately 2.7 million shares of our Class A common stock in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through one of the initial purchasers of the Convertible Notes or its affiliate at a purchase price per share equal to $105.71, the last reported sale price of our Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on June 22, 2026.
The Convertible Notes are carried at amortized cost. Debt issuance costs of approximately $30.6 million, which include underwriter discounts and offering expenses, are presented as a direct deduction from the carrying amount of the Convertible Notes and are amortized to interest expense over the contractual term of the Convertible Notes using the effective interest method. The effective interest rate of the Convertible Notes is 0.43%. The dilution impact was accounted for using the if-converted method; refer to Note 14 - Net Income (Loss) per Share for more information. As of September 30, 2026, the outstanding principal amount is $2.20 billion, and the net carrying amount is $2.17 billion.


As of September 30, 2026, the remaining unamortized debt issuance costs were $28.1 million with a remaining amortization period of approximately 3.01 years. As of September 30, 2026, the Convertible Notes are potentially convertible into 12.6 million shares of Class A common stock, and no shares were actually issued upon conversion.


The Indenture contains customary covenants and events of default, including non-payment of principal or interest when due, breach of other obligations, and cross-acceleration, each subject to grace periods and other terms specified in the Indenture. Upon such an event of default, the Convertible Notes may be declared immediately due and payable. The Indenture also sets forth certain bankruptcy or insolvency events of default involving the Company, after which the Convertible Notes become automatically due and payable. The Indenture also limits mergers, consolidations, and sales of all or substantially all assets of the Company, and imposes certain reporting obligations, among other things.


Settlement
We are required to settle any conversion by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the Convertible Notes being converted, with any excess settled in cash, shares of our Class A common stock, or a combination thereof, at our election.


Conversion
The Convertible Notes are convertible at the option of the holders, prior to the close of business on the business day immediately preceding July 1, 2029, if certain conditions related to their trading price or our share price are met, certain corporate events or distributions occur, or they are called for redemption.

Redemption
We may not redeem the Convertible Notes prior to July 1, 2028, except when the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Convertible Notes is less than $100 million and certain other conditions are satisfied.


We may redeem for cash all or any portion of the Convertible Notes (subject to certain limitations), at our option, on or after July 1, 2028 and prior to the twenty-first scheduled trading day immediately preceding the maturity date, if the last reported sale price of our Class A common stock has been at least 120% of the conversion price for a set period as specified in the Indenture, at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount of the Notes to be redeemed, plus any accrued and unpaid special interest, to, but excluding, the redemption date.


In the event of a fundamental change, holders may require the Company to repurchase the Convertible Notes at a repurchase price equal to 100% of the principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid special interest, if any.


Capped Calls Transactions
On June 22, 2026, in connection with the pricing of the Convertible Notes, and on June 23, 2026, in connection with the initial purchasers’ exercise in full of their option to purchase additional Convertible Notes, we entered into privately negotiated Capped Calls transactions with certain of the initial purchasers or their respective affiliates and certain other financial institutions at a cost of $123.2 million. For purposes of the RHM March 2026 Credit Agreement, the Alternate Base Rate is the greatest of (i) the prime rate then in effect, (ii) the Federal Reserve Bank of New York rate then in effect plus 0.5% and (iii) the Adjusted Term SOFR for a one month interest period plus 1.0%. Credit Card Funding Trust
Under terms of the Coastal Bank Program Agreement (discussed below), Robinhood Credit has the ability to purchase credit card receivables originated and held for a period of time by Coastal Bank. Robinhood Credit continues to earn interest from customers and uses these purchased credit card receivables as collateral under a trust structure to access debt financing in the ordinary course of business. To help facilitate these transactions, we created a VIE known as the Trust.
We are the primary beneficiary of the Trust as, through our role as the servicer and administrator, we have the power to direct the activities that most significantly affect the Trust’s economic performance and, due to owning all the equity interest in the Trust, have the right to receive benefits or the obligation to absorb losses. As such, we consolidate the Trust in the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements. Substantially all of the Trust’s assets and liabilities are the purchased credit card receivables, included in Receivable from users, net, the outstanding borrowings, included in Other current liabilities, and the Series 2026-1 asset-backed notes, included in Long-term borrowings, on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets.
Our exposure to losses in the Trust is limited to the carrying value of net assets held by the Trust, including expected credit losses related to the purchased credit card receivables (Refer to Note 7 - Allowance for Credit Losses). For the Trust, the creditors have no recourse to our general credit and the liabilities of the Trust can only be settled by the Trust’s assets. Additionally, the assets of the Trust can only be used to settle obligations of the Trust.
As of September 30, 2026, the Trust maintained six revolving borrowing arrangements (with Barclays, SVB, WF, Truist Bank, Goldman Sachs, and Mizuho) providing an aggregate commitment limit of $1.55 billion. Borrowings generally bear interest at a commercial paper rate, Term SOFR, or Daily Simple SOFR plus applicable margins ranging from 1.20% to 1.50%. Undrawn amounts accrue commitment fees between 0.20% and 0.35%. Coastal Bank Program Agreement
Under a program agreement between us and Coastal Bank (the “Program Agreement”) most recently amended in March 2026, Coastal Bank may fund up to $500 million of credit card receivables. Transaction Settlement


Our users have ownership of the securities they transact on our platforms, including those that collateralize margin loans, and, as a result, such securities are not presented on our unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets. In the normal course of business, we engage in activities involving settlement and financing of securities transactions. User securities transactions are recorded on a settlement date basis. The settlement date for equities and options is one business day after the trade date. These activities may expose us to off-balance sheet risk in the event that the other party to the transaction is unable to fulfill its contractual obligations. In such events, we may be required to purchase financial instruments at prevailing market prices in order to fulfill our obligations.
